features.title: Its install sheet asks only for what it uses — Claude Code on the user's AI profiles, About me, the microphone in its own view, the speech server's address ("tts"), public web pages, a schedule — and never for a folder or for skipping permission checks; its listing gives its summary

Add → a link: Echo reads the page itself (`ctx.web.read`), Claude only sorts out what is the article (menus, newsletter, related posts dropped); the article is queued, then fetching → writing (retelling, memo, fact check, terms) → voicing → ready, its retelling's blocks anchored to the article's own elements
A page's pictures are saved by Echo with the article (`images/imgN.ext`), shown in the original, and the blocks that explain one are marked from the picture itself (a run with the picture, no tools)

A long article (over 15,000 characters of text) is cut into parts at headings, each an article of its own in one Library topic named after it ("… · part k of n"), each part's retelling and fact check within one Claude run
A PDF at a link: Echo downloads it and takes its text out (no model), Claude lays it out as elements; the pages asked for ("Pages of a PDF") are the ones taken

A file of the user's: "Choose a file…" (PDF, Word, PowerPoint, text; `echoctl plugin call retell start --file` the same) has its text taken out at once; a path typed in Add is refused with the hint to choose the file

Settings → From plugins → Retell voice: the speech server (any that speaks the OpenAI API) is online with its models listed, a voice and model picked, ▶ Listen plays a sample; a server that is down or refuses the key says so in the user's words

The voice of an article is made block by block on the speech server (`/v1/audio/speech`), the article is ready when all of it is voiced, and the player plays it with its words lit, the original beside it and its memo, terms, facts and questions

A question about the article is answered from it (its elements named); with "search the web" the part beyond it is checked on pages Echo opened — its sources only pages that opened, marked "CHECKED ON PAGES ECHO OPENED", else "GENERAL KNOWLEDGE · NO PAGE COULD CONFIRM IT"
The fact check (setting "factcheck": fix) reports a claim of the retelling that isn't in the article and corrects its block before it is voiced
Practice → Make a quiz from what was listened to: a multiple-choice or true/false answer is checked at once, a written answer gets the coach's feedback in the language of explanations

Practice → Start a talk: a spoken talk in Echo's window — the coach's greeting voiced, what the user says written down (Realtime transcription), the coach answers in the same Claude conversation (`resume`, streamed), a stretch over the coach's voice judged and the coach stops for it; Finish saves the talk and its review
Reading lists: Claude names candidate pages, Echo opens each one, Claude picks the list only from those that opened (a page that is gone never in it); Keep puts it in Library as a topic
My phrases: a phrase saved gets a card (its meaning, when it is said, an example) in the language of explanations (setting "explain_lang"), and comes back for review when due
Text from pages, files and speech is shown as text, never as markup, in the player, Library and Practice; a page's instructions are never followed (they reach Claude only as data, with no tools)
The speech server's API key (a secret setting) is never shown, kept in the plugin's store or logged, and is sent only to the speech server
Every Claude run the plugin makes has no tools (`--tools ""`): reading, sorting, retelling, checking, answering, the coach — Echo opens pages and files, Claude only gets their text
A page Echo can't read (gone, not a web page) or a Claude run that fails puts the article in error with why, in the user's words; the rest of the queue goes on
Removing the plugin with its data takes its store and its Claude conversations with it
On the real OpenAI API with a person's own key: the voice, ▶ Listen, a spoken quiz answer and a live talk with a real microphone and headphones
Installed from the onetest marketplace on a clean computer (Windows and macOS): the sheet, the first article from a link to its voice
